    StartersPippin's hobbit fry-upBacon, fried mushrooms, grilled tomatoes and marmalade toast, served mid-morningHow to make it8 rashers of bacon250g mushrooms, sliced30g butter, for frying2 tomatoes, halved8 slices of white bread40g butter, for the toast4 tbsp marmaladeGrill the bacon and tomatoes.Melt the butter for frying in a pan and fry the mushrooms until golden.Toast the bread and spread with the butter for the toast and the marmalade.Serve on a big platter.Farmer Maggot's gruyère stuffed mushroomsField mushrooms filled with garlic breadcrumbs and gruyère, roastedHow to make it4 large field mushrooms50g breadcrumbs2 cloves of garlic, crushed1 tsp fresh thyme leaves80g gruyere, grated30g butter, meltedHeat the oven to 200°C. Remove the mushroom stems.Mix the breadcrumbs, garlic, thyme, gruyere and butter.Pile into the caps and roast until bubbling.Rest briefly and serve.Black pudding and apple bitesSecond breakfast, as Pippin asked Aragorn.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsPrancing Pony pieBeef braised in Worcestershire and stock under puff pastry, with buttery mashHow to make it1kg beef chuck, diced2 tbsp vegetable oil2 onions, sliced1 tsp dried thyme375ml beef stock1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce2 tbsp plain flour1 sheet of puff pastry1 egg, beaten1kg potatoes, peeled50g butter300g peasBrown the beef in batches in the oil, then soften the onions with the thyme.Add the stock and Worcestershire sauce and braise until the beef is tender.Thicken with the flour, pour into a pie dish, top with pastry and brush with egg.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Boil and mash the potatoes with the butter and cook the peas.Bilbo's party crackling pork roastThe party under the tree with fireworksHow to make itAs written, serves 4Pork shoulder salted overnight and roasted until the crackling shatters, with apple and sage sauce, roast potatoes and buttered cabbage.Score the skin of a 2kg pork shoulder, rub with 1 tbsp salt and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Roast at 240°C for 30 minutes, then 170°C for 2.5 hours.Roast 1kg parboiled potatoes in the fat for the last hour.Simmer 3 chopped apples with 2 tbsp sugar, 30g butter and chopped sage until soft for sauce.Shred half a savoy cabbage and cook in butter for 5 minutes.Rest the pork 20 minutes and carve.SweetsShire seed cakeButtery loaf cake with caraway seeds, sliced thick and butteredHow to make it175g butter, softened175g caster sugar3 eggs225g self-raising flour2 tsp caraway seeds3 tbsp milkextra butter, to serveHeat the oven to 170°C and line a loaf tin.Beat the butter and sugar until pale, add the eggs, then fold in the flour, caraway seeds and milk.Bake in the loaf tin until a skewer comes out clean.Slice thick and spread with butter.Lembas honey shortbread in leavesThe elvish waybread from Lothlórien, wrapped in a leafHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick honey and almond shortbread squares scored with a cross, baked pale and wrapped in fresh leaves tied with string.Beat 250g soft butter with 80g caster sugar and 3 tbsp honey until pale.Mix in 300g plain flour, 60g almond meal and a pinch of salt to a soft dough.Press into a lined 20cm square tin, score into 9 squares with a cross on each and prick.Bake at 160°C for 35 to 40 minutes until just golden.Cut while warm, cool, then wrap each in a clean banana or vine leaf and tie with kitchen string.DrinksPrancing Pony hot buttered appleApple juice and black tea warmed with honey, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg, whisked with butterHow to make it800ml cloudy apple juice2 black tea bags200ml boiling water2 tbsp honey1 cinnamon stick4 whole cloves1 pinch of nutmeg2 egg yolks30g butterSteep the tea bags in the boiling water for 4 minutes, then remove.Warm the apple juice and tea with the honey, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg until steaming, never boiling.Whisk the yolks, whisk in a ladle of the hot mix, then whisk back into the pan with the butter and stir until slightly thickened.Pour into tankards.
